notes: The everyday word. 'Walang pera' = broke. 'Pera-pera lang yan' = it's just a matter of money.

examples.tl: Wala akong pera ngayon, sa sahod na lang.
examples.en: I have no money right now, after payday instead.

examples.tl: May pera ka ba pang-Grab?
examples.en: Do you have money for the Grab?

notes: 'Piso' = one peso / a one-peso coin. In Taglish amounts are usually 'X pesos' (bente pesos, 500 pesos).

examples.tl: Kulang ng piso, okay lang ba?
examples.en: It's one peso short, is that okay?

examples.tl: Dalawang daang pesos ang pamasahe sa Grab.
examples.en: The Grab fare was two hundred pesos.

notes: Rarely handled now; prices get rounded. 25 sentimo coins still show up as sukli in supermarkets.

examples.tl: Bente-singko sentimo lang ang sukli, 'wag na.
examples.en: The change is only twenty-five centavos, never mind.

notes: Drivers and sari-sari stores often lack sukli, so having barya matters. 'Barya-barya' = small amounts.

examples.tl: Puro barya ang laman ng wallet ko.
examples.en: My wallet is full of coins.

examples.tl: Pabarya naman ng isang daan, pang-jeep.
examples.en: Can you break a hundred into coins, for the jeep.

notes: Asked by drivers, cashiers and vendors when you hand over a big bill. 'Wala akong barya' = I have no change.

examples.tl: Boss, may barya ka? Wala akong sukli sa limang daan.
examples.en: Boss, got any change? I don't have change for five hundred.
examples.taglish: Boss, may barya ka? Wala akong sukli sa 500.

notes: 'Walang sukli' = no change available. 'Keep the change' = 'Sa 'yo na yung sukli.'

examples.tl: Kuya, yung sukli ko po.
examples.en: Sir, my change please.

examples.tl: Wala akong sukli sa isang libo, may mas maliit ka?
examples.en: I have no change for a thousand, got anything smaller?

notes: Noun and also 'paid' as an adjective: 'Bayad na' = already paid. 'Pambayad' = money to pay with.

examples.tl: Magkano ang bayad sa parking dito?
examples.en: How much is the parking fee here?

examples.tl: Bayad na yung order, GCash.
examples.en: The order is already paid, via GCash.

notes: Said when handing fare to a jeepney driver, often passed forward by other passengers. Add destination and headcount: 'Bayad po, dalawa, Ayala.'

examples.tl: Bayad po, isa lang, hanggang Guadalupe.
examples.en: Fare please, just one, to Guadalupe.

examples.tl: Pakiabot po ng bayad.
examples.en: Please pass my fare forward.

notes: Actor focus. 'Magbayad ng kuryente' = pay the electric bill.

examples.tl: Nagbayad na ako ng kuryente kanina sa GCash.
examples.en: I already paid the electricity earlier on GCash.

examples.tl: Saan ako magbabayad, sa kahera?
examples.en: Where do I pay, at the cashier?

notes: Object focus: the thing or person paid is the topic. 'Bayaran mo ako' = pay me.

examples.tl: Babayaran ko na yung utang ko sa 'yo sa Friday.
examples.en: I'll pay you back what I owe on Friday.

examples.tl: Binayaran ko na yung internet, 1,699 ulit.
examples.en: I paid the internet already, 1,699 again.

notes: 'May utang ako sa 'yo' = I owe you. 'Utang na loob' = debt of gratitude, a big cultural concept.

examples.tl: May utang pa ako kay Mark, dalawang libo.
examples.en: I still owe Mark two thousand.

examples.tl: Ilista mo muna, utang.
examples.en: Put it on my tab for now (sari-sari store).

notes: Specifically money or credit. 'Mangutang' is the same meaning, slightly more formal.

examples.tl: Umutang siya sa akin, hindi pa nagbabayad.
examples.en: He borrowed money from me, hasn't paid yet.

examples.tl: Ayokong umutang sa online lending app, ang laki ng interest.
examples.en: I don't want to borrow from an online lending app, the interest is huge.

notes: pa- + utang = 'let me borrow'. Casual, between friends; 'naman' softens it.

examples.tl: Pautang muna, bro, limang daan lang, babayaran ko sa sahod.
examples.en: Lend me five hundred for now, bro, I'll pay you on payday.

notes: Root for borrowing things. 'Hiram lang' = just borrowed, not mine.

examples.tl: Hiram lang 'tong charger, ibalik mo ha.
examples.en: This charger is just borrowed, return it okay.

notes: For objects. For money 'umutang' is more usual, though 'humiram ng pera' is fine too.

examples.tl: Pwede ba akong humiram ng payong? Umuulan.
examples.en: Can I borrow an umbrella? It's raining.

examples.tl: Humiram ako ng pera sa kapatid ko para sa deposit.
examples.en: I borrowed money from my sibling for the deposit.

notes: Object focus of humiram.

examples.tl: Hihiramin ko lang yung ballpen mo, saglit.
examples.en: I'll just borrow your pen for a sec.

notes: Causative: let someone borrow. Object focus is 'ipahiram' (Ipahiram mo sa kanya).

examples.tl: Nagpahiram ako ng pera sa kapatid ko, hindi pa bumabalik.
examples.en: I lent money to my sibling, it hasn't come back.

examples.tl: Ayaw niyang magpahiram ng motor.
examples.en: He doesn't want to lend his motorbike.

notes: pa- request form. Very common: 'Pahiram ng charger.' Not for money (use 'pautang').

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na 'ko.
examples.en: Let me borrow your charger, my battery's dying.

notes: Both the pay and the day it arrives. Government and many companies pay on the 15th and 30th.

examples.tl: Kailan ang sahod mo?
examples.en: When is your payday?

examples.tl: Sa 15 at 30 ang sahod namin.
examples.en: We get paid on the 15th and 30th.

notes: From Spanish sueldo. Interchangeable with sahod.

examples.tl: Maliit ang sweldo pero malapit sa bahay.
examples.en: The salary is small but it's close to home.

notes: From Spanish quincena. Pair: kinsenas (15th) and katapusan (end of month).

examples.tl: Sa kinsenas na lang ako magbabayad ng renta.
examples.en: I'll pay the rent on the 15th payday instead.

notes: Literally 'the end'. As payday talk: 'Katapusan na bukas.'

examples.tl: Katapusan na bukas, may pera na ulit.
examples.en: Tomorrow is month-end payday, money again.

notes: Also the pronoun kita (I...you: mahal kita) and 'see' (nakita). Context decides.

examples.tl: Malaki ang kita niya sa online selling.
examples.en: She earns a lot from online selling.

examples.tl: Kumikita siya ng mga 30k kada buwan sa BPO.
examples.en: He earns about 30k a month at the BPO.

notes: 'Magastos' = costly to keep / a big spender. 'Gastusin' = expenses (noun) too.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng gastos ko this month, ang dami kong binili.
examples.en: My expenses are huge this month, I bought so much.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang tubig sa gastos sa renta?
examples.en: Is water included in the rent costs?

notes: Object focus 'gastusin' (Gastusin mo na).

examples.tl: Huwag ka nang gumastos, ako na ang magbabayad.
examples.en: Don't spend anymore, I'll pay.

notes: 'Matipid' = thrifty (person or car). 'Tipid-tips' is a common magazine phrase.

examples.tl: Tipid na lang muna tayo hanggang sahod.
examples.en: Let's just be frugal until payday.

examples.tl: Matipid sa gas yung kotse ko.
examples.en: My car is fuel-efficient.

examples.tl: Nagtitipid ako kasi may babayaran akong visa extension.
examples.en: I'm cutting back because I have a visa extension to pay for.

notes: Also 'love / dear' (mahal kita). 'Ang mahal!' = so expensive. 'Mahalin' = to hold dear.

examples.tl: Ang mahal naman! Wala bang tawad?
examples.en: That's so expensive! No discount?

examples.tl: Mahal ang renta sa BGC kumpara sa Mandaluyong.
examples.en: Rent in BGC is expensive compared to Mandaluyong.

notes: Also 'to curse' (nagmura siya). 'Mura lang' = it's cheap. 'Pamura' = cheap option.

examples.tl: Mura lang sa Divisoria, pero mas convenient sa mall.
examples.en: It's cheap in Divisoria, but the mall is more convenient.

examples.tl: Saan mas mura ang gulay, Cartimar o sa palengke?
examples.en: Where are vegetables cheaper, Cartimar or the market?

notes: Senior citizens and PWDs get 20 percent off by law, so 'senior discount' is heard everywhere.

examples.tl: May diskwento ba kung cash?
examples.en: Is there a discount if I pay cash?

examples.tl: May senior citizen discount po kami, ID lang.
examples.en: We have a senior citizen discount, just show ID.

notes: The discount you get by haggling. Also 'forgiveness' (patawad). Expected at tiangges and markets, not in malls.

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad, ate? Tatlo ang kukunin ko.
examples.en: No discount, miss? I'm taking three.

examples.tl: Binigyan niya ako ng tawad kasi suki ako.
examples.en: She gave me a discount because I'm a regular.

examples.tl: Tumawad ka, mahal masyado yung presyo niya.
examples.en: Haggle, her price is too high.

examples.tl: Hindi ako marunong tumawad, nahihiya ako.
examples.en: I don't know how to haggle, I get shy.

notes: The standard haggling opener. Follow with 'Last price?' or 'Kung dalawa, magkano?'

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad, kuya? Suki na 'ko dito.
examples.en: No discount, kuya? I'm a regular here already.

examples.tl: Wala bang tawad? Last price na ba yan?
examples.en: No discount? Is that your last price?

notes: 'Presyuhan' = to put a price on. 'Last price' is the haggling phrase, said in English.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang presyo ng bigas.
examples.en: The price of rice went up again.

examples.tl: Magkano ang presyo nito kung wholesale?
examples.en: What's the price of this wholesale?

notes: Only for prices and amounts of money. 'Ilan' = how many. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much altogether.

examples.tl: Magkano 'to, ate?
examples.en: How much is this, miss?

examples.tl: Magkano ang isang kilo ng manga?
examples.en: How much is a kilo of mangoes?

notes: 'Maningil' = to collect payment; 'singilin' = bill someone. 'Ang laki ng singil' = the bill is huge.

examples.tl: Magkano ang singil sa kuryente mo this month?
examples.en: How much is your electric charge this month?

examples.tl: May singil sa delivery, 49 pesos.
examples.en: There's a delivery charge, 49 pesos.

notes: Object focus; the person billed is the topic. Actor focus is 'maningil'.

examples.tl: Sinisingil na ako ng admin para sa association dues.
examples.en: The admin is already billing me for the association dues.

notes: 'Official receipt' (OR) matters for warranties and tax. 'Pa-resibo' = can I have a receipt.

examples.tl: Pwede pa-resibo?
examples.en: Can I get a receipt?

examples.tl: Itago mo yung resibo para sa warranty.
examples.en: Keep the receipt for the warranty.

notes: The dominant e-wallet; accepted at carinderias, tricycle drivers, bills. Verb-ified: 'i-GCash', 'mag-GCash', 'na-GCash'.

examples.tl: GCash ka ba? I-send ko na lang.
examples.en: Are you on GCash? I'll just send it.

examples.tl: Na-GCash ko na, check mo.
examples.en: I've GCashed it already, check it.

notes: To a vendor: asks to pay by GCash. To a friend: asks them to send via GCash. Look for the QR code sign.

examples.tl: Pa-GCash na lang ako, wala akong cash.
examples.en: I'll just pay by GCash, I have no cash.

examples.tl: Pa-GCash na lang ng share mo sa dinner.
examples.en: Just GCash me your share of the dinner.

notes: Formerly PayMaya; the second big e-wallet, also a digital bank with high savings interest.

examples.tl: May Maya ka? Dun ako mag-send, wala akong GCash.
examples.en: Do you have Maya? I'll send there, I have no GCash.

notes: Also 'bench' (stress on the last syllable). Manila speakers say 'bank' or just the bank's name (BPI, BDO).

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa bangko bukas para mag-open ng account.
examples.en: I'm going to the bank tomorrow to open an account.

examples.tl: Sarado ang bangko sa Sabado hapon.
examples.en: Banks are closed Saturday afternoon.

notes: Said letter by letter. 'ATM card' = debit card. Non-bank ATMs charge a fee; 'may service fee'.

examples.tl: May ATM ba dito malapit? Mag-withdraw lang ako.
examples.en: Is there an ATM near here? I just need to withdraw.

examples.tl: Offline yung ATM, try natin sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: The ATM is offline, let's try the 7-Eleven.

notes: Standard Taglish verb. 'Pa-withdraw' at a GCash outlet = cash out.

examples.tl: Nag-withdraw ako kanina pero may 250 na fee.
examples.en: I withdrew earlier but there was a 250 fee.

examples.tl: Magwi-withdraw lang ako sa BPI sa Glorietta.
examples.en: I'll just withdraw at the BPI in Glorietta.

notes: 'I-deposit' (object focus) = deposit it. Spelled 'deposito' in Tagalog but spoken as English.

examples.tl: Mag-deposit ka sa account ko, i-send ko sa 'yo yung details.
examples.en: Deposit to my account, I'll send you the details.

notes: Covers money sent home and parcels. 'Pinadala' = what was sent. OFW culture word.

examples.tl: May padala ang anak niya galing Dubai buwan-buwan.
examples.en: Her child sends money from Dubai every month.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko yung padala sa Palawan Express.
examples.en: I'll pick up the remittance at Palawan Express.

notes: Object focus 'ipadala' (Ipadala mo sa akin). Used for money, parcels, and 'send me the file'.

examples.tl: Nagpadala ako ng pera sa kapatid ko sa probinsya.
examples.en: I sent money to my sibling in the province.

examples.tl: Magpapadala ako ng balikbayan box sa December.
examples.en: I'll send a balikbayan box in December.

notes: Said in English. 'Remittance center' = Palawan, Cebuana Lhuillier, Western Union; also pawnshops.

examples.tl: Dumaan ako sa remittance center para kunin yung padala.
examples.en: I stopped by the remittance center to get the money sent.

notes: 'Wala akong load' = I'm out of credit. 'Pa-load' = top me up. Sold at every sari-sari store and via GCash.

examples.tl: Wala akong load, pa-text naman.
examples.en: I have no phone credit, can you text for me?

examples.tl: Pa-load ng 100, Globe, 0917.
examples.en: Load me 100, Globe, 0917.

notes: magpa- because you have someone load you. 'Mag-load' also heard for loading yourself via app.

examples.tl: Magpapa-load lang ako sa tindahan, 50 lang.
examples.en: I'll just buy 50 of load at the store.

notes: Said by cashiers in English. Reply 'Card po' or 'Cash po'. Many small places are 'cash lang' or GCash only.

examples.tl: Cash or card po? — Card po, debit.
examples.en: Cash or card? — Card please, debit.

examples.tl: Cash lang po tanggap namin, walang card.
examples.en: We only accept cash, no cards.

notes: Said in English. 'Cash lang' = cash only. 'Cash out' at a GCash outlet = withdraw e-money.

examples.tl: May cash ka? Walang GCash yung tindahan.
examples.en: Do you have cash? The store has no GCash.

notes: Handing exact fare: 'Sakto po.' Also 'just right' for fit, timing or taste.

examples.tl: Sakto lang yung pera ko, walang sukli. — Okay lang, kuya.
examples.en: My money is just exact, no change needed. — That's fine.

examples.tl: Sakto po, bente.
examples.en: Exact amount, twenty.

notes: 'Kulang ng bente' = twenty short. 'Kulang-kulang' = roughly, a bit short. 'Nagkulang' = fell short.

examples.tl: Kulang ng bente yung bayad mo, boss.
examples.en: Your payment is twenty short, boss.

examples.tl: Kulang pa ako ng 2k para sa renta.
examples.en: I'm still 2k short for the rent.

notes: 'Sobra ng singko' = five over. 'Sobra-sobra' = way too much. Also intensifier: 'sobrang mahal'.

examples.tl: Sobra ng singko yung binigay mo, eto sukli.
examples.en: You gave five too much, here's the change.

examples.tl: Sobrang mahal ng parking sa BGC.
examples.en: Parking in BGC is way too expensive.

notes: 'Isang libo' = 1,000; 'tatlong libo' = 3,000. Taglish: '3k', 'three thousand'. Linker: dalawang libo.

examples.tl: Tatlong libo ang renta kada linggo? Mahal.
examples.en: Three thousand rent per week? Expensive.

examples.tl: Sampung libo ang deposit.
examples.en: The deposit is ten thousand.

notes: 'Isang daan' = 100, 'dalawang daan' = 200. Becomes 'raan' after a vowel: apat na raan, anim na raan. Also 'road / way'.

examples.tl: Limang daan ang bayad sa labada.
examples.en: The laundry costs five hundred.

examples.tl: Apat na raan lang ang Grab galing airport.
examples.en: The Grab from the airport was only four hundred.

notes: Spanish numbers are normal for money and time: uno, dos, tres... singko (5), diyes (10), kinse (15), bente (20), trenta (30), singkwenta (50), siyento (100).

examples.tl: Bente pesos ang pamasahe sa jeep? Ang mahal na.
examples.en: Twenty pesos for the jeep? That's gotten expensive.

examples.tl: Bente-singko ang isang pandesal dito.
examples.en: A pandesal is twenty-five here.

notes: Prices in markets are nearly always quoted in Spanish numbers. 'Isang daan' usually replaces 'siyento' though.

examples.tl: Singkwenta lang po ang isang kilo ng kamatis.
examples.en: A kilo of tomatoes is just fifty.

notes: 'Libre ko' = my treat. 'Manlibre' = to treat people. Also 'available': 'Libre ka ba bukas?'

examples.tl: Libre ko kayo ng kape mamaya, sahod ko.
examples.en: Coffee's on me later, it's my payday.

examples.tl: Libre ang delivery kung 500 pataas.
examples.en: Delivery is free for 500 and up.

notes: Kanya-kanyang bayad. Pronounced 'kay-kay-bee'. Opposite of 'libre ko' or 'sagot ko'.

examples.tl: KKB tayo mamaya ha, wala pa akong sahod.
examples.en: We each pay our own later okay, I haven't been paid yet.

notes: Sagot = answer / responsibility. 'Sagot ko na yan' = I'll cover that. 'Ako na' also means 'let me pay'.

examples.tl: Sagot ko na yung dinner, birthday ko naman.
examples.en: Dinner's on me, it's my birthday anyway.

notes: Also 'pipe' (same stress) and 'sugarcane' (stress on last syllable). In Taglish 'interest' is more common for loans; 'tubo' for profit.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng tubo ng credit card kung minimum lang ang bayad.
examples.en: Credit card interest is huge if you only pay the minimum.

examples.tl: Maliit lang ang tubo sa pag-reselling ng load.
examples.en: The profit from reselling load is small.

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng puhunan para sa maliit na milk tea business.
examples.en: I need capital for a small milk tea business.

notes: 'Naipon' = accumulated. 'Ipon challenge' is a popular savings game.

examples.tl: May ipon ako para sa emergency, konti lang.
examples.en: I have some savings for emergencies, just a little.

examples.tl: Naubos ang ipon ko sa hospital bill.
examples.en: My savings got used up on the hospital bill.

notes: Hyphen because the root starts with a vowel. Object focus 'ipunin' (Ipunin mo yung barya).

examples.tl: Nag-iipon ako para sa bakasyon sa Palawan.
examples.en: I'm saving up for a vacation in Palawan.

examples.tl: Mag-ipon ka na, malapit na ang Pasko.
examples.en: Start saving, Christmas is near.

notes: Said in English; 'badyet' in formal spelling. 'Budget meal' = cheap set meal. 'Over budget' as-is.

examples.tl: Ang budget ko lang for rent ay 25k.
examples.en: My budget for rent is only 25k.
examples.taglish: 25k lang ang budget ko for rent.

examples.tl: May budget meal dito, 99 pesos with drinks.
examples.en: They have a budget meal here, 99 pesos with drinks.

notes: 'Hulog' = one installment / a deposit. Appliances and phones are often 'hulugan' at Home Credit.

examples.tl: Hulugan lang yung cellphone ko, 12 months, zero interest.
examples.en: My phone is on installment, 12 months, zero interest.

examples.tl: Pwede bang hulugan 'to?
examples.en: Can I pay for this in installments?

notes: Literally 'to drop'. Used for SSS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth contributions and for installment payments.

examples.tl: Maghuhulog ako sa SSS bukas, voluntary ako.
examples.en: I'll pay my SSS contribution tomorrow, I'm a voluntary member.

notes: 'Palitan ng pera' = money changer. Also the verb 'palitan' (to replace/change) and 'palitan' with mid stress (swap with each other).

examples.tl: Saan ang magandang palitan ng dolyar dito sa Makati?
examples.en: Where's a good dollar changer here in Makati?

examples.tl: Mas maganda ang rate sa palitan kaysa sa bangko.
examples.en: The rate is better at the money changer than the bank.

notes: Everyday speech often just says 'dollar(s)'. 'Ilan ang dolyar?' = what's the dollar rate.

examples.tl: Ilan ang dolyar ngayon? — Mga 57 na.
examples.en: What's the dollar at now? — About 57.

examples.tl: Magpapalit ako ng dolyar sa Sanry's.
examples.en: I'll change dollars at Sanry's.

notes: Said in English, or just 'rate'. 'Mataas ang dolyar' = the peso is weak.

examples.tl: Mataas ang exchange rate ngayon, magpapalit na ako.
examples.en: The exchange rate is high today, I'll exchange now.

examples.tl: Anong rate niyo sa dollar?
examples.en: What's your dollar rate?

notes: 'Magpalit ng dolyar' = change dollars; 'magpalit ng damit' = change clothes. Object focus 'palitan' / 'ipalit'.

examples.tl: Magpapalit ako ng 200 dollars, pwede sa mall.
examples.en: I'll exchange 200 dollars, can do it at the mall.

examples.tl: Nagpalit ako ng SIM, Smart na ako.
examples.en: I changed SIM, I'm on Smart now.

notes: Said in English. 'Mag-open ng account'. 'Account number' is asked for transfers; 'account name' too.

examples.tl: May account ka ba sa BPI? Dun ko i-transfer.
examples.en: Do you have a BPI account? I'll transfer there.

examples.tl: Anong account name, para hindi ma-bounce?
examples.en: What's the account name, so it doesn't bounce?

notes: English pronunciation. 'Check balance' at ATMs. Also for load: 'balance ng load'.

examples.tl: Check mo muna yung balance mo bago mag-withdraw.
examples.en: Check your balance first before withdrawing.

examples.tl: Maintaining balance ang hinahanap ng bangko, 3k.
examples.en: The bank requires a maintaining balance, 3k.

taglish: I-transfer mo na lang sa GCash ko.
notes: Used as noun and Taglish verb: 'i-transfer', 'nag-transfer', 'na-transfer na'. InstaPay = instant, PESONet = same day.

examples.tl: I-transfer mo na lang sa GCash ko, same number.
examples.en: Just transfer it to my GCash, same number.

examples.tl: Na-transfer na ba? Wala pa akong notification.
examples.en: Has it been transferred? I haven't gotten a notification.

notes: Said in English. 'Mag-invest', 'nag-invest'. Scam warning: 'investment scam' is a common news phrase.

examples.tl: Nag-invest ako sa mutual fund, maliit lang, 5k monthly.
examples.en: I invested in a mutual fund, just small, 5k monthly.

examples.tl: Baka scam yan, ang laki ng promised return.
examples.en: That might be a scam, the promised return is huge.

notes: 'Tax' is more common in speech; 'buwis' in news and formal. VAT is 12 percent and usually included in the price.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang buwis sa presyo?
examples.en: Is tax already included in the price?

examples.tl: Ang laki ng tax na kinakaltas sa sahod ko.
examples.en: The tax deducted from my salary is huge.

notes: 'Kinaltas' = was deducted. 'Bawas' is the general word for 'less/reduced'.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng kaltas sa sahod ko: tax, SSS, PhilHealth.
examples.en: The deductions from my salary are huge: tax, SSS, PhilHealth.

notes: You paid from your own money, usually unexpectedly. 'Mag-abono' = to advance the money.

examples.tl: Abonado ako sa dinner kagabi, hindi nagbayad si Mark.
examples.en: I was out of pocket for dinner last night, Mark didn't pay.

notes: 'Mag-ambag' = chip in. Common for group gifts, office parties, inuman.

examples.tl: Ambag tayo para sa gift ni boss, 200 each.
examples.en: Let's chip in for the boss's gift, 200 each.

notes: Prefix: pang-jeep, pang-gas, pang-kain, pang-rent = money for that. Spelling shifts: pam- before b/p (pambayad), pan- before d/t/s.

examples.tl: Wala akong pang-jeep, pahiram ng bente.
examples.en: I have no jeep money, lend me twenty.

examples.tl: Eto, pang-gas mo.
examples.en: Here, for your gas.

notes: Fare for jeep, bus, tricycle, Grab. 'Pamasahe' also = money you give someone for their trip.

examples.tl: Magkano ang pamasahe papuntang Cubao?
examples.en: How much is the fare to Cubao?

examples.tl: Tumaas ang pamasahe sa jeep, 15 na ang minimum.
examples.en: Jeep fare went up, minimum is 15 now.

notes: Said in English. Not mandatory; 'service charge' often on restaurant bills. 'Pang-tip' = tip money.

examples.tl: Bigyan mo ng tip yung rider, umulan pa.
examples.en: Give the rider a tip, it even rained.

examples.tl: Sa 'yo na yung sukli, tip.
examples.en: Keep the change, that's your tip.

notes: Often softened with 'ngayon' or 'muna'. 'Broke ako' and 'petsa de peligro' (days before payday) are common jokes.

examples.tl: Wala akong pera hanggang kinsenas, KKB tayo.
examples.en: I have no money until the 15th, we each pay our own.

examples.tl: Petsa de peligro na, wala na akong pera.
examples.en: Danger days before payday, I'm out of money.

notes: Say it to the guard or rider when a delivery is prepaid, or to a cashier when the app already charged you.

examples.tl: Bayad na yung order, kuya, GCash. — Okay, thank you po.
examples.en: The order's already paid, via GCash. — Okay, thank you.

notes: Ask before assuming something is free: parking, delivery, printing at the admin office.

examples.tl: May bayad ba yung delivery? — Wala, free na.
examples.en: Is there a delivery charge? — No, it's free.

examples.tl: May bayad ba ang pag-xerox dito sa admin?
examples.en: Is there a charge for photocopying here at the admin?

notes: 'Walang kuryente' = power's out. 'Bill sa kuryente' or just 'Meralco' = the electric bill. 'Nakuryente' = got shocked.

examples.tl: Nagbayad ka na ba ng kuryente? Due na bukas.
examples.en: Have you paid the electricity? It's due tomorrow.

examples.tl: Walang kuryente sa buong building, generator lang.
examples.en: No power in the whole building, just the generator.

notes: Metro Manila's electric utility; the name stands for the bill itself. Pay via GCash, Bayad Center or 7-Eleven.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng Meralco namin, 6k, dahil sa aircon.
examples.en: Our electric bill is huge, 6k, because of the aircon.

notes: Filipino English for any outage, scheduled or not. 'Nag-brownout' = the power went out.

examples.tl: Brownout kanina ng dalawang oras, nainitan ako sa condo.
examples.en: Power was out for two hours earlier, I got hot in the condo.

notes: As a utility: 'bill sa tubig', Manila Water or Maynilad. 'Walang tubig' = water's cut. Also drinking water.

examples.tl: Magkano ang bill sa tubig niyo kada buwan?
examples.en: How much is your water bill per month?

examples.tl: Walang tubig bukas 10 to 4, may repair daw.
examples.en: No water tomorrow 10 to 4, there's a repair.

notes: Providers: PLDT, Globe, Converge. 'Mabagal ang internet' is a daily complaint. 'Wi-Fi' said 'wai-fai'.

examples.tl: Ang bagal ng internet, tatawag ako sa Converge.
examples.en: The internet is so slow, I'll call Converge.

examples.tl: Kasama na ba ang internet sa renta?
examples.en: Is internet included in the rent?

notes: 'Bayarin' is the Tagalog, but speech uses 'bill(s)'. In a restaurant: 'Bill out po' or 'Chit po'.

examples.tl: Ang dami kong bills this month: Meralco, tubig, internet.
examples.en: I have so many bills this month: electric, water, internet.

examples.tl: Bill out na po tayo.
examples.en: Can we have the bill please.

examples.tl: Ang dami kong bayarin bago mag-Pasko.
examples.en: I have so many bills to pay before Christmas.

notes: Said in English; 'due na' = it's due. 'Overdue' and 'penalty' also English.

examples.tl: Kailan ang due date ng credit card mo?
examples.en: When is your credit card due date?

examples.tl: Due na bukas yung Meralco, bayaran ko na ngayon.
examples.en: The electric bill is due tomorrow, I'll pay it now.

notes: Monthly fee for common areas, billed by the admin per square meter. Usually paid by the owner, but check your lease.

examples.tl: Tumaas ulit ang association dues sa building namin.
examples.en: The association dues in our building went up again.

examples.tl: Sino ang magbabayad ng dues, ako o yung may-ari?
examples.en: Who pays the dues, me or the owner?

notes: 'Upa' is the Tagalog; 'renta' and 'rent' are what Manila says. 'Magrenta' = to rent.

examples.tl: Magkano ang renta sa condo mo sa BGC?
examples.en: How much is the rent on your condo in BGC?

examples.tl: Kasama na sa renta ang dues at parking.
examples.en: Dues and parking are included in the rent.

notes: 'Umupa' = rent from; 'paupahan' = for rent; 'inuupahan' = being rented. Also hiring: 'upahan' = hired (killer, in news).

examples.tl: Dalawang buwan nang hindi nagbabayad ng upa yung kapitbahay.
examples.en: The neighbor hasn't paid rent for two months.

notes: Taglish 'mag-rent' is just as common. 'Magpaupa' = to rent out.

examples.tl: Umuupa lang kami, hindi amin yung unit.
examples.en: We're just renting, the unit isn't ours.

notes: Seen on signs: 'Paupahan: Room for rent'. 'Apartment for rent' also as-is.

examples.tl: May paupahan daw sa Poblacion, 15k kada buwan, studio.
examples.en: There's a place for rent in Poblacion, 15k a month, studio.

notes: Lease, job contract, phone plan. 'Kontraktwal' = contractual worker, a political buzzword.

examples.tl: One year ang kontrata, tapos renewable.
examples.en: The contract is one year, then renewable.

examples.tl: Basahin mo muna ang kontrata bago pumirma.
examples.en: Read the contract first before signing.

notes: Standard lease ask: 'two months deposit, one month advance'. In speech it's 'deposit', English pronunciation.

examples.tl: Two months deposit at one month advance ang hinihingi ng landlord.
examples.en: The landlord is asking for two months deposit and one month advance.

examples.tl: Ibabalik ba ang deposito pagkatapos ng kontrata?
examples.en: Will the deposit be returned after the contract?

notes: may + ari (possession). Used for unit owners, store owners, dog owners. 'Sino ang may-ari?' = whose is this?

examples.tl: Tatawagan ko ang may-ari, sira yung aircon.
examples.en: I'll call the owner, the aircon is broken.

examples.tl: Nasa abroad ang may-ari, broker ang kausap ko.
examples.en: The owner is abroad, I deal with the broker.

notes: Said in English; 'landlady' for women. 'Kasera/kasero' is the old Tagalog word, now mainly in boarding houses.

examples.tl: Strict yung landlord ko sa visitors, pa-register sa guard.
examples.en: My landlord is strict about visitors, they register with the guard.

notes: From Spanish casera. 'Kasero' for a man. Mostly in bedspace and boarding house talk, less for condos.

examples.tl: Si Aling Nena ang kasera namin, mabait pero mahigpit sa bayad.
examples.en: Aling Nena is our landlady, kind but strict about payment.

notes: Both 'broker' and 'agent' used. Many condo units are listed by agents on Facebook groups.

examples.tl: May kilala kang broker? Naghahanap ako ng unit sa Salcedo.
examples.en: Do you know a broker? I'm looking for a unit in Salcedo.

notes: 'Lipat-bahay' = house move; 'lipat-bahay truck' is the moving service. Also change jobs: 'lumipat ng company'.

examples.tl: Lilipat kami sa Makati next month, mas malapit sa trabaho.
examples.en: We're moving to Makati next month, closer to work.

examples.tl: Lumipat siya ng kumpanya, mas mataas ang offer.
examples.en: He moved companies, the offer was higher.

notes: Address as 'kuya guard' or 'boss'. Guards receive packages, log visitors, and know everything about the building. 'Sekyu' is slang.

examples.tl: Iwan mo lang sa guard yung package, kukunin ko mamaya.
examples.en: Just leave the package with the guard, I'll get it later.

examples.tl: Kuya guard, may rider sa labas, pa-GCash lang yung bayad.
examples.en: Kuya guard, there's a rider outside, payment is just GCash.

accept_tl: May package ba para sa akin?
notes: Ask the lobby guard or receptionist. Add unit number: 'para sa 1204'. 'Dumating' = arrived.

examples.tl: Kuya, may dumating ba na package para sa Unit 1204?
examples.en: Kuya, did a package arrive for Unit 1204?

examples.tl: May dumating ba na Lazada? Pirma lang ako.
examples.en: Did a Lazada delivery come? I'll just sign.

notes: The condo's property management office: dues, gate passes, move-in permits, complaints. 'Sa admin' = go to the admin.

examples.tl: Sa admin mo i-report yung tumutulo sa CR.
examples.en: Report the leak in the bathroom to the admin.

examples.tl: Kumuha ka ng gate pass sa admin para sa movers.
examples.en: Get a gate pass from the admin for the movers.

notes: Building handymen for plumbing, electrical, aircon. Request through admin; small tip appreciated.

examples.tl: Tumawag ako sa maintenance para sa aircon cleaning.
examples.en: I called maintenance for the aircon cleaning.

notes: 'Nasira' = broke down. 'Sirain' = to break something. 'Sira-ulo' = crazy (slang).

examples.tl: Sira yung lock ng pinto, pa-ayos sa landlord.
examples.en: The door lock is broken, have the landlord fix it.

examples.tl: Sira ang elevator ulit, hagdan tayo.
examples.en: The elevator is broken again, stairs it is.

notes: Also 'to sort out' paperwork: 'Aayusin ko ang visa ko.' 'Pa-ayos' = have it fixed. 'Ayos' = okay, in order.

examples.tl: Aayusin daw ng maintenance yung gripo bukas.
examples.en: Maintenance will fix the faucet tomorrow.

examples.tl: Aayusin ko muna ang papeles ko sa immigration.
examples.en: I'll sort out my immigration papers first.

notes: 'Ma-cut' / 'na-cut' for utilities and internet; 'naputol' is the Tagalog. 'Disconnection notice' comes in English.

examples.tl: Bayaran mo na ang internet, baka ma-cut.
examples.en: Pay the internet now, it might get cut off.

examples.tl: Na-cut yung Meralco namin, hindi nabayaran.
examples.en: Our electricity got cut, it didn't get paid.

notes: Actor focus. Object focus is 'bilhin'. 'Pabili' = please buy for me / I'd like to buy (at a counter).

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng ulam sa carinderia, tapos umuwi.
examples.en: I bought food at the carinderia, then went home.

examples.tl: Bibili ako ng tubig sa 7-Eleven, gusto mo?
examples.en: I'll buy water at 7-Eleven, want some?

notes: Object focus; the item is the topic. Irregular: bilhin, not bilihin.

examples.tl: Bibilhin ko yung sapatos kung may sale.
examples.en: I'll buy the shoes if there's a sale.

examples.tl: Saan mo binili yung bag mo? Ganda.
examples.en: Where did you buy your bag? Nice.

accept: I'd like to buy / please buy for me
notes: At a sari-sari store window: 'Pabili po ng Coke.' To a friend going out: 'Pabili ng yosi' = buy me cigarettes.

examples.tl: Pabili po ng isang Coke sakto at yelo.
examples.en: I'd like a Coke sakto and some ice please.

examples.tl: Pabili ng softdrinks pag dumaan ka sa tindahan.
examples.en: Buy me a soda when you pass the store.

notes: Vendors shout 'Bili na kayo!' 'Magkano bili mo?' = how much did you pay. 'Pabili' = please buy.

examples.tl: Magkano bili mo dito? Mukhang mahal.
examples.en: How much did you pay for this? Looks expensive.

notes: mang- + bili. Forms: namili, namimili, mamimili. Also 'to choose' (mamili ka = pick one). Taglish: 'mag-shopping'.

examples.tl: Mamimili ako sa Landmark mamaya, may kulang sa kusina.
examples.en: I'll go shopping at Landmark later, the kitchen is missing some things.

examples.tl: Mamili ka, alin ang gusto mo?
examples.en: Choose, which one do you want?

notes: Usually means the sari-sari store on the corner. 'Tinda' = goods for sale; 'magtinda' = to sell.

examples.tl: Bumili ka ng yelo sa tindahan sa kanto.
examples.en: Buy ice at the store on the corner.

examples.tl: Sarado na ang tindahan, 10 PM na.
examples.en: The store is closed, it's 10 PM.

notes: Tindero for a man. Address them as 'ate' / 'kuya', or 'ma'am/sir' in malls.

examples.tl: Tanong mo sa tindera kung may size 10.
examples.en: Ask the saleslady if they have size 10.

notes: 'Cashier' is just as common. 'Sa kahera' / 'sa counter' = pay over there.

examples.tl: Sa kahera na po kayo magbayad, dun po.
examples.en: Please pay at the cashier, over there.

notes: 'Mag-mall' = hang out at the mall, the national pastime. SM, Ayala (Glorietta, Greenbelt), Robinsons.

examples.tl: Tara sa Greenbelt, mag-mall tayo, ang init sa labas.
examples.en: Let's go to Greenbelt, hang out at the mall, it's hot outside.

notes: 'Naka-sale' = on sale. '3-day sale', 'midnight sale', '11.11' online. 'Sale' pronounced as in English.

examples.tl: May sale sa SM, 50% off ang mga damit.
examples.en: There's a sale at SM, clothes are 50% off.

notes: 'Naka-' = in the state of. Also 'Kasama ba sa sale?' = is this included in the sale.

examples.tl: Ate, naka-sale ba 'to o regular price?
examples.en: Miss, is this on sale or regular price?

notes: English word. 'Anong size mo?' Shoe sizes are US sizes; clothes run small, so XL is normal for Americans.

examples.tl: May size medium ba nito?
examples.en: Do you have this in medium?

examples.tl: Anong size mo sa sapatos? — 10.
examples.en: What's your shoe size? — 10.

notes: 'Anong kulay?' 'May ibang kulay?' Colors: pula, asul/blue, berde/green, dilaw, itim, puti.

examples.tl: May ibang kulay ba? Ayoko ng pula.
examples.en: Is there another color? I don't want red.

notes: 'Sukatin' = measure; 'magsukat/isukat' = try on. 'Sakto ang sukat' = fits exactly.

examples.tl: Sakto ang sukat, hindi masikip.
examples.en: The fit is just right, not tight.

examples.tl: Anong sukat ng kama? Queen?
examples.en: What's the bed size? Queen?

notes: Object focus 'isukat' (Isukat mo muna). 'Pwede bang magsukat?' is the fitting room ask.

examples.tl: Pwede bang magsukat? Saan ang fitting room?
examples.en: Can I try it on? Where's the fitting room?

examples.tl: Isukat mo muna bago bilhin, baka masikip.
examples.en: Try it on first before buying, it might be tight.

notes: English. Staff may limit items: 'tatlo lang po'.

examples.tl: Saan po ang fitting room? Isusukat ko lang.
examples.en: Where's the fitting room? I'll just try it on.

notes: Clothes fit and crowding: 'masikip sa MRT'. 'Sikip' root.

examples.tl: Masikip sa baywang, may mas malaki ba?
examples.en: It's tight at the waist, is there a bigger one?

examples.tl: Ang sikip sa jeep, siksikan.
examples.en: The jeep is so cramped, packed.

notes: Opposite of masikip. Also 'relaxed, lenient' (maluwag ang boss) and 'traffic is light'.

examples.tl: Maluwag yung large, kunin ko na lang yung medium.
examples.en: The large is loose, I'll just take the medium.

notes: 'No return, no exchange' signs are illegal under consumer law but exchange-only is common in practice. Keep the resibo.

examples.tl: Pwede ba mag-refund kung may defect?
examples.en: Can I get a refund if it's defective?

examples.tl: Store credit lang daw, walang cash refund.
examples.en: They said store credit only, no cash refund.

notes: 'I-exchange', 'pa-exchange'. Usually within 7 days with receipt and tags.

examples.tl: Pwede bang i-exchange, mali yung size?
examples.en: Can I exchange it, the size is wrong?

examples.tl: Seven days lang ang exchange, dalhin mo yung resibo.
examples.en: Exchange is only within seven days, bring the receipt.

notes: Ask about stock or seconds. 'Meron' is spoken 'mayroon'. Answer: 'Meron pa' / 'Ubos na'.

examples.tl: Meron pa ba nito sa size large? — Ubos na po.
examples.en: Do you still have this in large? — All sold out.

examples.tl: Meron pa bang kanin? Pa-extra rice.
examples.en: Is there more rice? Extra rice please.

notes: 'Naubusan ako' = I missed out, they ran out on me. 'Out of stock' also said in English.

examples.tl: Ubos na po yung pandesal, bukas na ulit.
examples.en: The pandesal is all gone, tomorrow again.

examples.tl: Naubusan ako ng tickets, ang bilis.
examples.en: I missed out on tickets, they went so fast.

notes: A two-way loyalty bond: the suki buyer gets tawad and extras, the suki seller gets repeat business. Also used as address: 'Suki!'

examples.tl: Suki na ako dun, binibigyan ako ng tawad.
examples.en: I'm a regular there, they give me a discount.

examples.tl: Suki, bili ka na, sariwa 'to.
examples.en: Regular, buy some, this is fresh.

notes: Greenhills, Divisoria 168, Christmas bazaars. Haggling expected. Pronounced chang-ge.

examples.tl: Sa tiangge sa Greenhills, tumawad ka lagi, mataas ang unang presyo.
examples.en: At the Greenhills bazaar, always haggle, the first price is high.

notes: Fresh meat, fish, vegetables. 'Mamalengke' = go to market. Go early; bring cash and barya.

examples.tl: Mas mura ang gulay sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.
examples.en: Vegetables are cheaper at the market than the supermarket.

examples.tl: Mamalengke tayo sa Guadalupe bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: Let's go to the Guadalupe market tomorrow morning.

notes: Market pricing is per kilo. 'Kalahating kilo' = half kilo. 'Isang kilo ng...' with linker ng.

examples.tl: Magkano ang kilo ng bangus?
examples.en: How much per kilo for bangus?

examples.tl: Kalahating kilo lang ng baboy, pakigiling.
examples.en: Just half a kilo of pork, please grind it.

notes: The sachet economy: shampoo by the sachet, cigarettes by the stick, eggs by the piece. 'Tingi-tingi' = little by little.

examples.tl: Tingi lang ang bili ko ng shampoo, sachet.
examples.en: I buy shampoo by the piece, in sachets.

notes: A vendor's stall or anyone's assigned spot. 'Pumwesto' = take your spot.

examples.tl: May pwesto siya sa tiangge sa Baclaran, damit.
examples.en: She has a stall at the Baclaran market, clothes.

notes: Default payment for Shopee and Lazada. Pronounced see-oh-dee. Have exact cash ready for the rider.

examples.tl: COD na lang yung order ko sa Shopee, wala akong card.
examples.en: My Shopee order is cash on delivery, I have no card.

examples.tl: COD po ba 'to? Magkano babayaran?
examples.en: Is this COD? How much do I pay?

notes: Grab, Lalamove, Shopee, J&T riders on motorbikes. They call or text 'nasa lobby na po ako'. Tip: 'pang-tip'.

examples.tl: Nasa lobby na daw yung rider, may bayad ba?
examples.en: The rider's in the lobby, is there payment due?

examples.tl: Tumawag yung rider, hindi makahanap ng building.
examples.en: The rider called, he can't find the building.

notes: 'Umorder' also common. 'I-order' = order it. 'Order na tayo' = let's order.

examples.tl: Nag-order ako sa GrabFood, 30 minutes daw.
examples.en: I ordered on GrabFood, 30 minutes they said.

examples.tl: Mag-oorder pa ba kayo o bill out na?
examples.en: Are you ordering more or shall we get the bill?

notes: paki- = please. For leftovers or gifts. 'Take-out' is the usual word for food to go; 'balot' for wrapping.

examples.tl: Pakibalot po yung natira, iuuwi ko.
examples.en: Please wrap up the leftovers, I'll take them home.

examples.tl: Pakibalot na pang-gift, may ribbon.
examples.en: Please gift-wrap it, with a ribbon.

notes: 'Anong trabaho mo?' = what do you do. Taglish uses 'work' heavily: 'nagwo-work ako', 'may work ako bukas'.

examples.tl: Anong trabaho mo? — Nagwo-work ako remote, IT.
examples.en: What's your job? — I work remote, IT.

examples.tl: Maraming trabaho sa BPO sa Ortigas at BGC.
examples.en: There are lots of jobs at BPOs in Ortigas and BGC.

notes: Taglish equivalent 'mag-work / nag-work / nagwo-work'. 'Pumasok' is more common for 'go to work'.

examples.tl: Nagtatrabaho siya sa BPO sa Ortigas, night shift.
examples.en: She works at a BPO in Ortigas, night shift.

examples.tl: Nagtrabaho ako sa Saudi ng limang taon.
examples.en: I worked in Saudi for five years.

notes: 'Office' is what most people say. 'Officemate' = coworker.

examples.tl: Nasa opisina pa ako, late na uuwi.
examples.en: I'm still at the office, I'll go home late.

examples.tl: Saan ang office niyo? — Sa Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: Where's your office? — On Ayala Avenue.

notes: Also a friendly address for strangers: guards, drivers, vendors ('Boss, magkano?'). 'Bossing' is the jokey version.

examples.tl: Mabait ang boss ko, pero strict sa deadline.
examples.en: My boss is nice, but strict about deadlines.

examples.tl: Boss, pakibukas ng gate.
examples.en: Boss, please open the gate.

notes: Used for employers of household staff, drivers, OFWs abroad. For office bosses, 'boss'. 'Maamo' (different word) = tame.

examples.tl: Mabait ang amo ng kasambahay namin dati.
examples.en: Our helper's former employer was kind.

examples.tl: Hindi nagbabayad ng tama ang amo niya sa Dubai.
examples.en: Her employer in Dubai doesn't pay properly.

notes: ka- = companion in. Taglish: 'kawork', 'officemate', 'teammate'.

examples.tl: Katrabaho ko siya dati sa Makati, magkaibigan na kami.
examples.en: He was my coworker before in Makati, we're friends now.

examples.tl: Kasama sa trabaho ko si Jen, kaya kilala ko.
examples.en: Jen works with me, that's why I know her.

notes: English. 'May meeting ako', 'nasa meeting'. 'Mag-meeting' = hold a meeting.

examples.tl: May meeting ako ng 10, tawagan na lang kita pagkatapos.
examples.en: I have a meeting at 10, I'll just call you after.

notes: English. 'Bukas ang deadline', 'lagpas sa deadline' = past the deadline.

examples.tl: Bukas ang deadline, kaya mag-OT ako ngayon.
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow, so I'm doing overtime today.

notes: 'Mag-leave' = take leave; 'mag-file ng leave'. SL = sick leave, VL = vacation leave. Pronounced as in English.

examples.tl: Mag-leave ako sa Friday, may lakad kami sa Tagaytay.
examples.en: I'm taking leave on Friday, we have a trip to Tagaytay.

examples.tl: Nag-file na ako ng VL, approved na.
examples.en: I filed my vacation leave, it's approved.

notes: 'Off ako bukas' = I'm off tomorrow. 'Rest day' used in shift work.

examples.tl: Day off ko bukas, matutulog lang ako buong araw.
examples.en: It's my day off tomorrow, I'll just sleep all day.

examples.tl: Anong off mo? — Lunes at Martes.
examples.en: What are your days off? — Monday and Tuesday.

notes: Almost always 'OT' (oh-tee). 'Nag-OT', 'may OT pay', 'forced OT'.

examples.tl: Nag-OT ako kagabi hanggang 10, grabe.
examples.en: I did overtime last night until 10, intense.

examples.tl: May OT pay ba kayo o wala?
examples.en: Do you get overtime pay or not?

notes: Standard Taglish verb. 'Applicant' and 'application' as-is.

examples.tl: Nag-apply ako sa tatlong kumpanya, isa ang tumawag.
examples.en: I applied to three companies, one called back.

examples.tl: Mag-aapply ako ng credit card sa BPI.
examples.en: I'll apply for a credit card at BPI.

notes: English, usually pronounced 'rez-yoo-may'. Jobs sites: JobStreet, Indeed, LinkedIn.

examples.tl: I-send mo yung resume mo sa HR email, i-refer kita.
examples.en: Send your resume to the HR email, I'll refer you.

notes: English. 'Ma-interview' = get interviewed. 'Final interview', 'initial interview'.

examples.tl: May interview ako bukas, kinakabahan ako.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, I'm nervous.

notes: The key admin word. Every office posts a list of requirements; bring photocopies of everything. 'Kumpleto ba ang requirements mo?'

examples.tl: Ano ang requirements para sa barangay clearance?
examples.en: What are the requirements for a barangay clearance?

examples.tl: Kulang ang requirements ko, bumalik ako bukas.
examples.en: My documents were incomplete, I'll come back tomorrow.

notes: Pronounced eye-dee. 'Valid ID' = government-issued. Guards ask 'ID po' for visitors and often keep it until you leave.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang dalawang valid ID at photocopy.
examples.en: Bring two valid IDs and photocopies.

examples.tl: ID po, sir, para sa visitor pass.
examples.en: ID please, sir, for the visitor pass.

notes: 'Lagda' is the formal word on forms. 'Pirma dito' = sign here.

examples.tl: Pirma dito, tapos petsa sa tabi.
examples.en: Sign here, then the date next to it.

notes: Object focus 'pirmahan' (Pirmahan mo ang kontrata). Taglish 'mag-sign' also common.

examples.tl: Pumirma ka dito sa baba ng form.
examples.en: Sign here at the bottom of the form.

examples.tl: Pirmahan mo muna ang logbook sa guard.
examples.en: Sign the logbook at the guard first.

notes: 'Fill-out-an mo yung form' or 'i-fill out' are standard Taglish. 'Application form', 'ballpen' needed, black ink.

examples.tl: Fill-out-an mo yung form tapos ibigay sa window 3.
examples.en: Fill out the form then give it to window 3.

notes: 'Punan' is the Tagalog for fill in. Forms: 'Punan ang lahat ng patlang' = fill in all blanks.

examples.tl: I-fill out mo muna 'to bago pumila.
examples.en: Fill this out first before lining up.

examples.tl: Na-fill out ko na, kulang lang ng pirma.
examples.en: I've filled it out, it just needs a signature.

notes: 'Ang haba ng pila' = the line is long. 'Pumila' = to line up. 'Singit' = cutting in line, a big sin.

examples.tl: Ang haba ng pila sa BIR, umaga pa ako dito.
examples.en: The line at the BIR is so long, I've been here since morning.

examples.tl: Saan ang pila para sa renewal?
examples.en: Where's the line for renewals?

examples.tl: Pumila ka muna dun para kumuha ng number.
examples.en: Line up over there first to get a number.

examples.tl: Pumipila na ako sa labas ng 6 AM.
examples.en: I was already lining up outside at 6 AM.

notes: Government offices and banks give a queue number first. 'Kumuha ng number', 'tinawag na ang number ko'.

examples.tl: Kumuha ka muna ng number sa guard sa entrance.
examples.en: Get a number from the guard at the entrance first.

examples.tl: Tinawag na ba ang number ko? 47.
examples.en: Has my number been called? 47.

notes: Clerks call 'Sunod!' 'Susunod' = the next one / upcoming (susunod na linggo = next week). 'Sumunod' = to follow.

examples.tl: Sunod! — Ako po.
examples.en: Next! — That's me.

examples.tl: Sino ang susunod sa pila?
examples.en: Who's next in line?

notes: Government offices route you by numbered windows. 'Sa window 5 ang releasing.'

examples.tl: Sa window 5 po ang releasing, dun kayo pumila.
examples.en: Releasing is at window 5, line up there.

notes: Pronounced bee-eye-ar. TIN = tax ID number; 'RDO' = your revenue district office. Freelancers register here.

examples.tl: Kukuha ako ng TIN sa BIR, kailangan sa bank account.
examples.en: I'll get a TIN at the BIR, it's needed for the bank account.

notes: Private-sector pension system; 'hulog sa SSS' = contribution. GSIS is the government-employee version. Pag-IBIG = housing fund.

examples.tl: Automatic ang hulog ko sa SSS, kinakaltas sa payroll.
examples.en: My SSS contribution is automatic, deducted from payroll.

notes: Covers part of hospital bills; foreigners with ACR can enroll voluntarily. 'May PhilHealth ka ba?' is asked at admission.

examples.tl: Gamitin mo ang PhilHealth mo sa hospital para may bawas.
examples.en: Use your PhilHealth at the hospital so there's a deduction.

notes: Barangay = smallest local government unit. Get it at the barangay hall; needed for leases, jobs, police clearance. 'Cedula' often with it.

examples.tl: Kailangan ng barangay clearance para sa lease at sa bangko.
examples.en: You need a barangay clearance for the lease and the bank.

examples.tl: Saan ang barangay hall ng Poblacion?
examples.en: Where's the Poblacion barangay hall?

notes: Pronounced en-bee-eye. Online appointment required; 'hit' means a name match delays release. Needed for jobs and visas.

examples.tl: May appointment ako para sa NBI clearance sa Lunes, sa Robinsons.
examples.en: I have an appointment for my NBI clearance Monday, at Robinsons.

examples.tl: May hit daw ang NBI ko, balik after one week.
examples.en: My NBI had a name hit, come back after a week.

notes: Say it to the guard to skip the walk-in line. Add time and office: 'ng 9 AM sa immigration'. 'Walk-in' is also said.

examples.tl: May appointment ako sa immigration ng 9 AM, saan ang pila?
examples.en: I have a 9 AM appointment at immigration, where's the line?

examples.tl: Walk-in po ba kayo o may appointment?
examples.en: Are you a walk-in or do you have an appointment?

notes: Main office in Intramuros; satellite offices in SM Aura, Robinsons and others handle extensions. 'BI' pronounced bee-eye.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa immigration sa Intramuros para sa extension.
examples.en: I'm going to immigration in Intramuros for the extension.

examples.tl: Mas mabilis sa BI satellite office sa mall.
examples.en: It's faster at the BI satellite office in the mall.

notes: English. 'Tourist visa', '9(a)', '13(a)' spouse visa, 'SRRV' retiree visa, 'expired na ang visa'.

examples.tl: Kailan expire ang visa mo?
examples.en: When does your visa expire?

examples.tl: Nag-apply ako ng 13(a) visa kasi kasal ako sa Pilipina.
examples.en: I applied for a 13(a) visa because I'm married to a Filipina.

notes: 'Mag-extend', 'nag-extend', 'mag-e-extend' = extend the visa. Tourist extensions run 1 or 2 months at a time.

examples.tl: Mag-e-extend ako ng visa, dalawang buwan ulit.
examples.en: I'll extend my visa, two months again.

examples.tl: Magkano ang extension ngayon? Tumaas daw.
examples.en: How much is the extension now? They say it went up.

notes: Alien Certificate of Registration. Required after 59 days; renew yearly with the annual report in January. Guards accept it as valid ID.

examples.tl: Dalhin mo ang ACR I-Card mo pag magre-renew ka.
examples.en: Bring your ACR I-Card when you renew.

examples.tl: January ang annual report, dalhin ang ACR.
examples.en: The annual report is in January, bring the ACR.

notes: 'Expired' said in English for IDs, visas, food. 'Paso' is the Tagalog but rare in speech. 'Ma-expire' = to expire.

examples.tl: Expired na yung ID ko, kailangan i-renew.
examples.en: My ID has expired, it needs renewing.

examples.tl: Baka ma-expire ang visa ko bago makuha ang ACR.
examples.en: My visa might expire before I get the ACR.

notes: Passports (DFA), licenses (LTO), leases, ACR. Object focus 'i-renew'.

examples.tl: Magre-renew ako ng lease, pero hihingi ako ng tawad sa renta.
examples.en: I'll renew the lease, but I'll ask for a discount on rent.

examples.tl: Nag-renew siya ng passport sa DFA Aseana.
examples.en: She renewed her passport at DFA Aseana.

notes: Every government and bank transaction has one. 'Express lane fee' at immigration is a legit extra for faster service.

examples.tl: May processing fee na 500 pesos, cash lang.
examples.en: There's a processing fee of 500 pesos, cash only.

notes: 'Releasing' is the pickup window. 'Kailan ang release?' = when can I pick it up. 'Na-release na' = ready.

examples.tl: Release daw ng clearance sa Wednesday, balik ako.
examples.en: The clearance is released Wednesday, I'll come back.

examples.tl: Na-release na ang ACR mo, pwede nang kunin.
examples.en: Your ACR has been released, you can pick it up.

notes: Generic for photocopy, pronounced 'seroks'. 'Pa-xerox' = please copy. Xerox stalls sit outside every government office.

examples.tl: Pa-xerox ng ID, dalawang kopya, front and back.
examples.en: Photocopy my ID please, two copies, front and back.

examples.tl: May xerox sa labas, 3 pesos per page.
examples.en: There's a photocopier outside, 3 pesos per page.

notes: 'Dalawang kopya' = two copies. 'Kumopya' = to copy / cheat on a test.

examples.tl: Dalawang kopya ng form, isa sa 'yo, isa sa kanila.
examples.en: Two copies of the form, one for you, one for them.

notes: 'Pa-notaryo' / 'i-notarize'. Leases, affidavits and authorization letters need it; notaries cluster near city halls.

examples.tl: Pa-notaryo ng kontrata, 200 pesos lang sa tabi ng city hall.
examples.en: Get the contract notarized, just 200 pesos next to city hall.

notes: Someone who offers to speed up paperwork for a fee, illegal under the Anti-Red Tape Act. Signs say 'No to fixers'.

examples.tl: Wag kang kumuha ng fixer, bawal yan at baka ma-scam ka.
examples.en: Don't get a fixer, it's illegal and you might get scammed.

notes: 'Company' more common in speech. 'Pinapasukan' = the company you work at.

examples.tl: Anong kumpanya ang pinapasukan mo?
examples.en: What company do you work for?

notes: 'May pasok' = there's work/class; 'walang pasok' = suspended (holiday, typhoon). Also 'come in': 'Pasok!'

examples.tl: May pasok ba bukas? — Wala, holiday.
examples.en: Is there work tomorrow? — No, it's a holiday.

examples.tl: Walang pasok sa Metro Manila dahil sa bagyo.
examples.en: No work or classes in Metro Manila because of the typhoon.

en: to go to work or school / enter
notes: The everyday verb for going to work. 'Hindi ako pumasok' = I didn't go in / I was absent.

examples.tl: Papasok ako ng 9, pero traffic sa EDSA.
examples.en: I go in at 9, but EDSA has traffic.

examples.tl: Hindi ako pumasok kahapon, may sakit ako.
examples.en: I didn't go to work yesterday, I was sick.

notes: English. 'Regular holiday' = double pay; 'special non-working'. Government offices and banks close; malls stay open.

examples.tl: Holiday sa Lunes, sarado ang mga government office.
examples.en: Monday is a holiday, government offices are closed.

examples.tl: Long weekend! Holiday sa Friday.
examples.en: Long weekend! Friday is a holiday.

notes: Mandatory extra month of salary paid by December 24. Pronounced 'thirteenth month'. 'Pang-Pasko' money.

examples.tl: Sa December ang 13th month, pang-Pasko at pang-ipon.
examples.en: The 13th month pay comes in December, for Christmas and savings.

notes: English. HMO (health card), rice allowance, 13th month, SL/VL. 'Regular' status after six months probation unlocks them.

examples.tl: May HMO at rice allowance sa benefits, kaya tinanggap ko.
examples.en: The benefits include an HMO and rice allowance, so I accepted.

notes: From 'racket' but neutral: a side job or one-off paid gig. 'May raket ako' = I've got a gig. 'Nagraraket' = hustling.

examples.tl: May raket ako sa weekends, nagtuturo ng English online.
examples.en: I have a side gig on weekends, teaching English online.

notes: Filipino English for a second income source. 'Sideline ko' = my side job.

examples.tl: Sideline ko ang pag-Grab tuwing gabi, pandagdag sa renta.
examples.en: Driving Grab at night is my side job, to help with rent.

notes: 'Mag-negosyo' = go into business. 'Negosyante' = businessperson. Small businesses: milk tea, sari-sari store, online selling.

examples.tl: Gusto kong mag-negosyo, maliit na cafe sa Poblacion.
examples.en: I want to start a business, a small cafe in Poblacion.

notes: 'Nawalan ng' = lost (something). 'Natanggal' = got removed/fired. 'Na-laid off' and 'na-retrench' also heard.

examples.tl: Nawalan siya ng trabaho noong pandemic, ngayon nag-Grab.
examples.en: He lost his job during the pandemic, now he drives Grab.

notes: Key admin verb: kumuha ng number, ng clearance, ng ID. Object focus 'kunin' (Kunin mo). 'Pakuha' = please get.

examples.tl: Kukuha ako ng barangay clearance bukas ng umaga.
examples.en: I'll get a barangay clearance tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: Kumuha ka ng number sa guard bago pumila.
examples.en: Get a number from the guard before lining up.

notes: Object focus of kumuha. Irregular: kunin, not kuhain. 'Kukunin ko mamaya' = I'll pick it up later.

examples.tl: Kukunin ko yung package sa guard mamaya.
examples.en: I'll pick up the package from the guard later.

examples.tl: Kinuha na ba niya ang sukli?
examples.en: Did he take the change already?

notes: Forms, requirements, reports: 'ipasa sa window 2'. Also pass the ball / the salt. 'Mag-submit' is the Taglish option.

examples.tl: Ipasa mo yung form sa window 2, tapos hintayin ang pangalan mo.
examples.en: Submit the form at window 2, then wait for your name.

examples.tl: Ipinasa ko na ang requirements ko sa HR.
examples.en: I already submitted my requirements to HR.

notes: Offices, stores, roads. 'Sarado pag lunch' = closed at lunch, common in government offices. 'Isara' = to close.

examples.tl: Sarado ang BIR pag lunch, 12 to 1, kumain muna tayo.
examples.en: The BIR is closed at lunch, 12 to 1, let's eat first.

examples.tl: Sarado na ang bangko, 3 PM lang.
examples.en: The bank is already closed, only until 3 PM.

notes: Stress distinguishes: bukas with final stress (open) vs first-syllable stress (tomorrow). Context clears it. 'Buksan' = to open.

examples.tl: Bukas ba ang bangko sa Sabado? — Bukas, hanggang 12.
examples.en: Is the bank open Saturday? — Open, until 12.

examples.tl: Bukas pa ang tindahan, bilis.
examples.en: The store is still open, hurry.

notes: On forms: 'Petsa' next to 'Lagda'. 'Anong petsa ngayon?' = what's the date. 'Petsa de peligro' = broke days before payday.

examples.tl: Lagay mo ang petsa ngayon sa tabi ng pirma.
examples.en: Put today's date next to the signature.

notes: English. 'Performance bonus', 'Christmas bonus' (separate from the mandatory 13th month). 'May bonus ba kayo?'

examples.tl: May bonus kami sa December kung maabot ang target.
examples.en: We get a bonus in December if we hit the target.

notes: English for the bank product; 'ipon' for the money itself. Digital banks (Maya, GoTyme, CIMB) pay higher interest than BDO/BPI.

examples.tl: Mag-open ka ng savings sa digital bank, mataas ang interest.
examples.en: Open a savings account at a digital bank, the interest is high.

notes: English in everyday talk; 'tubo' in Tagalog. 'Zero interest' installment deals are everywhere. 'Patubuan' = money lending at interest.

examples.tl: Zero interest kung 6 months installment sa card.
examples.en: Zero interest if it's 6 months installment on the card.

examples.tl: Ang laki ng interest ng 5-6, iwasan mo.
examples.en: The interest on 5-6 lending is huge, avoid it.

notes: Core cultural value: a favor creates a lasting obligation to repay. 'Walang utang na loob' = ungrateful, a serious insult.

examples.tl: Malaki ang utang na loob ko sa kanya, tinulungan niya ako nung wala akong trabaho.
examples.en: I owe him a big debt of gratitude, he helped me when I had no job.

en: Put it on my tab for now.
notes: Sari-sari store credit: the owner keeps a 'listahan' (notebook) of what you owe, paid on payday. Only for suki.

examples.tl: Ate, ilista mo muna, sa Sabado ko babayaran.
examples.en: Ate, put it on my tab for now, I'll pay Saturday.

notes: 'Chit' is an old Filipino English word for the restaurant bill. 'Bill out' is the common alternative. Make a signing gesture in the air.

examples.tl: Chit po, tapos pa-separate yung sa amin.
examples.en: The bill please, and separate ours.
